correlates.name: Ventricular Escape Rhythm (Escape Beats)
correlates.presentation: A very slow rhythm, in the range of 20-40 bpm from His-Purkinje tissue; under strong vagal stimulation the lecturer specifies a rate under 40 bpm.
correlates.pathophysiology: Failure of both the sinus node and the AV node to generate impulses removes overdrive suppression, unmasking the latent pacemaker channels in the His-Purkinje system.

correlates.name: Sinus Tachycardia and Sinus Bradycardia
correlates.presentation: Normal adult sinus rate is 60-100 bpm (average about 72 bpm). A sinus rate above 100 bpm is sinus tachycardia; below 60 bpm is sinus bradycardia.
correlates.pathophysiology: Both are disorders of the rate of sinus node phase 4 depolarization (or of the distance to threshold). Sympathetic drive steepens phase 4 and speeds the rate; vagal drive hyperpolarizes and flattens phase 4 and slows it.

correlates.name: Atrial Fibrillation (and the AV Node as a Protective Filter)
correlates.presentation: The resulting ventricular rate is far slower than the atrial rate, typically 100-150 bpm during AF.
correlates.pathophysiology: During atrial fibrillation the atrial rate is 400-600 bpm. Because the AV node conducts slowly and has a long refractory period, many atrial impulses are blocked within the node.

correlates.name: Bundle Branch Block (Left or Right)
correlates.presentation: Although normal His and bundle branch activation is invisible on the ECG, bundle branch block CAN be diagnosed on the ECG - because it alters the ventricular activation sequence, and the ventricular activation sequence is what the QRS displays.
correlates.pathophysiology: Loss of conduction down one bundle branch forces the affected ventricle to be activated late, by slow cell-to-cell muscle conduction from the contralateral ventricle rather than by the fast Purkinje network.

transporters.name: HCN Channel (Funny Current, I_f)
transporters.location: SA node, and to a lesser degree AV node and His-Purkinje tissue
transporters.function: The main driver of phase 4 spontaneous depolarization — a non-selective cation current carrying Na+ and K+ that generates automaticity
transporters.regulation: Opens on hyperpolarization below about -65 mV and is directly modulated by cyclic nucleotides, so sympathetic stimulation steepens the phase 4 slope and vagal tone flattens it
transporters.inhibitor: Ivabradine, which slows heart rate without touching contractility

transporters.name: I_KACh (Acetylcholine-activated K+ Channel)
transporters.location: SA node, atria and AV node
transporters.function: Opening it hyperpolarizes the pacemaker cell, moving the maximum diastolic potential further from threshold and slowing the rate
transporters.regulation: Activated by vagal acetylcholine at M2 receptors through the G-protein beta-gamma subunit
transporters.inhibitor: Atropine, by blocking the muscarinic receptor upstream

formulas.name: Pacemaker Hierarchy
formulas.equation: SA node 60-100 bpm, AV node 40-60 bpm, His-Purkinje 20-40 bpm
formulas.meaning: The fastest site suppresses the slower ones by overdrive suppression; an escape rhythm surfaces only when the sites above it fail or vagal tone is overwhelming
formulas.normalValue: Escape beats at 20-40 bpm indicate the ventricle is pacing itself

formulas.name: Cardiac Conduction Velocities
formulas.equation: Purkinje 2-4 m/s > His and bundle branches 2 m/s > atria and ventricles 0.5-1 m/s > AV node 0.01-0.05 m/s
formulas.meaning: The AV node is deliberately the slowest link, creating the delay that lets the atria finish emptying before the ventricles contract
formulas.normalValue: The SA node itself conducts at only about 0.01 m/s

formulas.name: Determinants of Pacemaker Rate
formulas.equation: Rate = distance / speed, where distance is maximum diastolic potential to threshold and speed is the phase 4 slope
formulas.meaning: Vagal stimulation attacks all three levers at once — it hyperpolarizes through I_KACh while reducing I_f and I_Ca to flatten the slope, which is why acetylcholine is such a powerful brake
formulas.normalValue: A flatter slope, a more negative maximum diastolic potential, or a less negative threshold all slow the rate

formulas.name: Intrinsic Heart Rate
formulas.equation: Intrinsic HR (both autonomic limbs blocked) is about 100 bpm; resting HR is about 70 bpm
formulas.meaning: Because the heart runs slower at rest than when denervated, parasympathetic tone must be dominant at rest
formulas.normalValue: Both intrinsic heart rate and maximum heart rate (220 - age) decline with age

formulas.name: The Three Autonomic Tropies
formulas.equation: Chronotropic = rate; dromotropic = conduction; inotropic = contractility
formulas.meaning: Sympathetic stimulation increases all three, vagal stimulation decreases all three — the vocabulary for every autonomic effect on the heart
formulas.normalValue: Vagal effects are strongest on the SA and AV nodes; sympathetic effects reach the ventricular myocardium as well
